key_insight: By automatically synthesizing large-scale open-ended forecasting questions from daily news and training reasoning-capable LMs (Qwen3) on that data (OpenForesight), the paper scales language-model-based prediction of future events while controlling for temporal leakage.
problem_solved: Addresses the scarcity of large, high-quality training/evaluation data for open-ended forecasting and the risk of future-information leakage when training models to reason about future events.
method: Automatically synthesize forecasting questions from global news reports using a careful, fully automated curation pipeline to scale data (OpenForesight).
Train and adapt the Qwen3 ‘thinking’ models on the synthesized dataset to elicit open-ended future predictions.
Prevent leakage of future information via offline dataset snapshots and temporal partitioning / evaluation protocols that respect news timelines.
impact: Provides a scalable dataset and protocol for training and evaluating models on open-ended forecasting, enabling practitioners to develop and benchmark temporal reasoning and prediction capabilities with better data hygiene.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: news articles → automated question synthesis → OpenForesight dataset → Qwen3 training → predictions
Timeline visualization showing offline snapshot / temporal splits to illustrate leakage prevention
Accuracy / calibration schematic comparing open-ended predictions (confidence vs. outcome) to convey uncertainty handling
Icon set: globe + clock (future), dataset cylinder (OpenForesight), neural net (Qwen3), shield (leakage protection)
paper_title: Scaling Open-Ended Reasoning to Predict the Future
paper_authors: Nikhil Chandak, Shashwat Goel, Ameya Prabhu, Moritz Hardt, Jonas Geiping
